content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services at 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center by calling 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current medical condition. It should not be used for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver function tests, should be conducted prior to initiating this medication and periodically during its use to monitor for potential side effects or complications. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. The information provided here is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Note that itraconazole interacts with many medications, and other drugs may affect how itraconazole is metabolized and eliminated from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Contact the relevant plan provider for the most up-to-date information.
